title: Agents: user collectors + Go connection settings card
head: fb906927c5b3
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Go auth cookie file can be world-readable, including after updates to an existing permissive file
leads.consequence: Apply serializes the browser authCookie in plaintext under HOME/.config/omarchy/agents/opencode-go.json without setting owner-only mode. Quickshell uses QSaveFile for atomicWrites; Qt creates new files with 0666 & umask (typically 0644) and copies an existing file's permissions on replacement. Atomicity is not secrecy. Anyone who can read that user's permissive directory and file can obtain the cookie. Create or chmod it 0600 before saving, and verify the mode after each replacement.

leads.summary: Apply starts a fetch before the Go config save completes and ignores save failures
leads.consequence: With a normal asynchronous FileView.setText, the next line starts --force opencode before saved() fires. A collector that reads config may fetch with old credentials, leaving the new cookie saved afterward with no retry. If save fails, onSaveFailed is unhandled and printErrors is false; a previous valid record can even yield 'Saved.' although no config was saved. Wait for onSaved, handle onSaveFailed, then fetch.

leads.summary: Filters and retry target output IDs, but the updater filters collector group names
leads.consequence: For a multi-record collector named opencode emitting opencode-go, settings.providers['opencode-go'].enabled=false produces --except opencode-go, yet group opencode still runs on every timer/refresh and rewrites the hidden record. retryAdvised:true on that record triggers --limits-only opencode-go, which matches no collector and exits 0; the advised retry does not actually re-probe the source. Map output IDs to their owning group or pass a group filter to the producer.

leads.summary: A zero-record collector cannot retire all its old tabs, and switching to a single record also leaves old IDs
leads.consequence: {} is valid output when a multi-account source has no accounts left, but it fails the nonempty-map test and exits 1 before fan_out can retire anything. A later single-id record follows the single branch and likewise never updates the producer sidecar or removes the other file. Removing a collector binary or deleting its sidecar has the same frozen-tab effect. In a synthetic run the old 'other.json' survived both changes. Accept the empty map as a valid retirement and handle every output-shape transition/deletion.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed by source (single-record branch never touches sidecar, updater lines 56-66; {} rejected confirmed in Opus matrix). Folded into id-handling finding as one sentence

leads.summary: Unvalidated map keys can overwrite other providers and later delete unrelated files, with success exit
leads.consequence: Output key claude is allowed in an opencode group and overwrites claude.json even if that file belonged to another collector. Key '../intrude' fails mktemp because the hidden temp parent does not exist, but errors do not make collect fail, and the key enters the sidecar; the next successful map omitting it invokes rm -f usage/../intrude.json and deletes a file outside usage. Synthetic run exits 0 for both attempts and deletes both the separate provider file and the higher-level file. Reject unsafe keys and mismatches with inner .id, namespace or coordinate ownership, and propagate failures.

leads.summary: Go config ignores XDG_CONFIG_HOME while collector discovery honors it
leads.consequence: If XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set to a path other than HOME/.config, Apply creates the Go JSON under HOME/.config while user collectors live under XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omarchy/agents/collectors. Any collector following Omarchy's usual XDG config pattern (the shipped fireworks collector uses it) will not read that saved cookie; prefill also reads the wrong path. Resolve one XDG-aware path in the panel and document it.

leads.summary: Parallel multi-record collectors can lose each other's producer ownership
leads.consequence: Every collector runs in a background job and does an unguarded read-modify-rename of the same update-producers.json. If groups A and B both read the original sidecar before either mv, the second rename loses the other's newly recorded IDs. Later retirement cannot find the lost IDs, so their usage files persist; overlapping IDs may be removed by one group while another writes them. Serialize the sidecar transaction and define collision ownership.

leads.summary: The Go Apply/Test target reaches neither shipped collectors nor either related OpenCode Go PR
leads.consequence: Both buttons invoke --force opencode. At this head only claude, codex and fireworks collectors exist, so the updater runs no job and exits 0. The open Go collectors in #8065 and #12651 are named omarchy-agent-usage-opencode-go (record id opencode-go), so merging either alone still does not refetch it; neither reads this PR's authCookie/workspaceId JSON. #12635 does add an opencode collector, but its record id is opencode, for which this card is hidden. Target the actual group and integrate the config contract with a named collector, or make the group configurable and report when no collector matched.

leads.summary: Related orphan-cleanup PR #10911 would delete idle multi-record tabs even while their user collector still exists
leads.consequence: The valid automatic merge (zero conflict markers) enumerates only packaged collector basenames and plugin scripts/bin, not this PR's ~/.config/omarchy/agents/collectors or the map keys they emit. Its final remove_orphans() deletes any output-id usage file not written within 7 days. If such a collector does not run for seven days (for example its group is explicitly excluded), its existing output-id tabs vanish despite the executable remaining installed; its migration applies the same rule. Teach the GC both producer sidecar IDs and user collector directory before these PRs combine.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator from #10911 diff (known_agents covers OMARCHY_PATH/bin and plugins dirs only; removes unknown records older than 7 days)

leads.summary: Related provider-toggle PR #11930 merges without a Git conflict but assigns PanelHero.trailingControl twice
leads.consequence: The clean text merge contains two bindings for the same PanelHero.trailingControl, one Go settings gear and one provider-switch gear. QML cannot give both controls the one slot; at minimum one feature is lost, and duplicate assignment may prevent Panel.qml loading. Compose both controls explicitly rather than treating a clean text merge as a functioning panel. Runtime load not exercised without a compositor.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator from #11930 diff (trailingControl: Component { Button ... } on the same PanelHero). Load outcome of a combined file not run; published as an integration overlap only

leads.summary: Related Claude multi-account PR #10080 uses a second record shape that requires explicit merge handling
leads.consequence: #10080's Claude collector emits a single record with id claude and nested accounts[], expecting the updater to write claude-work.json, strip the nested field and retire signed-out accounts. This PR's first branch classifies it as an ordinary single record and only writes claude.json. Automatic three-way merge has conflict markers in collect and fan_out; choosing only this PR's branch drops the other PR's extra tabs and fails its added agent-usage-update-test.sh. Integrate both formats deliberately if both merge.
leads.triage: ordinary textual conflict with a different feature; low value for this PR's author; omitted

leads.summary: Related user-collector PR #12353's packaged-wins tests are incompatible with this PR's duplicate execution
leads.consequence: This PR runs packaged and user collectors with the same group concurrently, both writing the same usage file; last rename wins. #12353 discovers the same user directory but deliberately deduplicates by group with packaged precedence and adds a test that the packaged 'good' record survives a user collector of the same name. The automatic merge has conflict markers over the registration loop. If the duplicated loop is retained, that test is nondeterministic or fails; agree on precedence and run each basename once.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator from #12353 diff (collectors map, packaged name wins, with tests); complements Opus F6

leads.summary: Existing updater/panel tests miss every new user-collector and Go settings path
leads.consequence: A plausible broken implementation that rejects an empty multi-record map or runs both packaged and user collectors with one name still passes all seven existing updater assertions; the Go panel test reads only launchAgent/right/middle click strings. Head tests pass while a synthetic empty-map output exits 1 and leaves stale files, and no test asserts that Apply waits for onSaved or that the target group exists. Add synthetic map, empty retirement, collision/precedence, disabled-id and save-result tests. Lower priority than the functional bugs.

flags.claim: An id containing `/` fails in `mktemp`, but the run still exits 0.
flags.why: Too broad. The id `/../../../../../escape` also contains `/` and was written, outside the usage directory; the draft says so in the previous sentence. Only `a/b` failed, because `$USAGE_DIR/.a/` does not exist. The exit-0 part is correct.

flags.claim: validate ids against the charset the panel already accepts
flags.why: Wrong source. The panel accepts any `*.json` file name as an agent id (Main.qml line 27, `find -name "*.json"`; lines 39-50; Agent path at line 59). The charset `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` I referred to is Main.qml's `safeDeviceId` (line 450), which is used for sync device ids.

flags.claim: Diagram: '-> after 800 ms, judge the previous record -> "Saved."'; Impact: 'a mismatch shows a false success'
flags.why: The verdict comes from the previous record. It is 'Saved.' only when that record is fresh (not stale, has limits, no status text). Otherwise the card shows the old failure reason. In the same harness, the Apply with the good cookie under the misnamed collector showed 'Expired cookie.', because the old record was stale.

flags.claim: A `retryAdvised` flag on a fan-out record never triggers a retry.
flags.why: `wanted()` compares the argument with the group name. A fan-out record whose id equals its group name (for example an `opencode` record from the `opencode` group) would still be retried. Only records whose id differs from the group are missed.

flags.claim: 'one group's entries are lost' (60 of 60 runs) and Impact 'it recreates the frozen-tab problem'
flags.why: Lost qualifier: each of the 60 iterations started from an empty sidecar (the loop runs `rm -f "$SIDE"`). With an existing sidecar, the last writer keeps what it read, so only that run's changes by the other group are lost. An id already recorded is still retired, because retirement uses the group's own read. Only an id that first appears in a run whose sidecar write is lost stays unretired, and a later uncontended run does not repair it.

flags.claim: 'creating the file with 0600 in the existing mkdir step when it is missing is enough, for example `install -m 600 /dev/null <path>`' and 'Starting the fetch from `onSaved` would also make the separate `mkdir` process unnecessary'
flags.why: The two suggestions conflict: the first puts the 0600 step in the mkdir process, the second removes that process. 'Is enough' also only covers new files: an existing 0644 file keeps 0644, because QSaveFile copies the existing mode. The 'when it is missing' condition matters. `install` over an existing file truncates it, and FileView skips `setText` when the text equals its cached content, so re-applying identical values would leave the file empty.

flags.claim: #10911: '...a user collector's records would be removed after a week without updates, for example while it is disabled.'
flags.why: This conflicts with the draft's own point (line 56) that disabling a fan-out id does not stop its collector, so those records keep updating. The example holds for a single-record user collector whose id equals its group, or for a collector that keeps failing for a week. The pruning mechanism itself is verified: 604800 s, and known names come only from `$OMARCHY_PATH/bin` and `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/*/{scripts,bin}`.

flags.claim: The README says a user collector can use any `<group>` name.
flags.why: Nitpick. The README gives the pattern `omarchy-agent-usage-<group>` and 'Target one group with ... --force <group>'. It names no required group, but it does not say 'any'.

flags.claim: 'a console session cookie copied from browser devtools' / 'The file holds an opencode.ai session cookie.'
flags.why: Nitpick. The PR calls it an 'auth cookie', and the hint points to opencode.ai > F12 > Application > Storage > Cookies. That it is the console session cookie is my inference; it was not verified, and no live service was contacted.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** with no user collectors, `omarchy-agent-usage-update` behaves as on the base for the packaged collectors: records are written byte-identically, and `--force`, `--limits-only`, `--except`, the per-agent filter and the exit status all match. `Panel.qml` loads without QML errors at this head and merged onto current `quattro` (no conflicts; `ShellIpc` carried over). Stock tabs keep their status box and full-opacity limits. The existing agent tests pass at this head.

The main open question is the Go settings card, which depends on a collector that is not in this PR. Smaller issues follow in the fan-out sidecar, cookie storage, filters and panel focus.

### Go card depends on an undocumented, out-of-tree collector contract

`Panel.qml` hard-codes a contract that no file in the PR produces or documents:

| Hard-coded in `Panel.qml` | Value |
|---|---|
| Provider id (line 97) | `opencode-go` |
| Apply/Test target (lines 163, 476) | `omarchy-agent-usage-update --force opencode` |
| Config file and schema (lines 98, 150) | `~/.config/omarchy/agents/opencode-go.json`, `{workspaceId, authCookie}` |
| Status words read (lines 187-192) | `expired`, `not connected`, `unavailable` |

The README describes user collectors as `omarchy-agent-usage-<group>` and names no required group. If the Go collector is named anything other than `opencode`, Apply and Test run nothing, the updater exits 0, and the card judges the old record. In a synthetic run with a collector named `omarchy-agent-usage-go`, Apply with a wrong cookie reported "Saved." with undimmed meters; the collector only ran on the next panel refresh, which then showed "Expired cookie.".

```text
Apply -> write opencode-go.json -> update --force opencode
      -> no collector named "opencode" -> exit 0, no record written
      -> after 800 ms, judge the previous record -> "Saved." if it was fresh
```

It also overlaps with open PRs that add packaged OpenCode collectors:
- #8065 and #12651 add `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-opencode-go` emitting id `opencode-go`. If either lands, this gear appears on that stock tab and hides its red status box, but Apply writes a file that collector does not read, and `--force opencode` does not refresh it.
- #12635 adds a packaged `omarchy-agent-usage-opencode`, the same name this card targets (see the name-collision note below).

Those collectors read Go limits from OpenCode's `/zen/go/v1/usage` endpoint with the API key OpenCode already stores, rather than an opencode.ai auth cookie copied from browser devtools.

**Impact:** "zero behavior change for stock installs" holds only while no packaged collector emits `opencode-go`. For user collectors, the card works only when the collector matches an unwritten contract, and a mismatch can show a false success.

**Suggested change:** ship the Go collector together with the card, or split the PR so the generic user-collector support lands on its own. Document the config file, record fields and status words in the README. Derive the Apply/Test target from the producer sidecar (id to group) or from the record, instead of hard-coding `opencode`, and report "no collector ran" when nothing matched.

### Parallel collectors lose entries in the producer sidecar

`fan_out` runs inside each backgrounded `collect … &` (updater line 107) and does an unlocked read, merge and rename of `update-producers.json` (lines 83-97). When two multi-record user collectors finish together, one group's sidecar update is lost; with two fast synthetic groups starting from an empty sidecar this happened in 60 of 60 runs. An id first emitted in a run whose update is lost is never recorded, so when the group later stops emitting it, its usage file is not retired, even after later runs without contention. Ids already recorded in an earlier run were still retired.

**Impact:** limited to users with two or more multi-record collectors, but for newly added ids it recreates the frozen-tab problem the sidecar is meant to prevent.

**Suggested change:** serialize the sidecar step with `flock` on a lock file next to it, or collect each group's ids and do retirement and the sidecar update once after the `wait` loop.

### Auth cookie is saved world-readable

`goConfigFile.setText()` goes through Quickshell's FileView and `QSaveFile`, which creates a new file with mode 0666 minus umask. Under umask 022 the measured result was `opencode-go.json` at 0644 inside a 0755 directory. The file holds the opencode.ai auth cookie.

**Impact:** other local users can read the cookie wherever the home directory permissions allow it; 0600 is the usual mode for a credential file.

**Suggested change:** `QSaveFile` keeps an existing file's mode (a pre-created 0600 file stayed 0600 after `setText`, and an existing 0644 file stays 0644). Before `setText`, create the file with mode 0600 when it is missing and `chmod 600` it when it already exists.

### Disabling or retrying a fan-out provider targets the wrong name

`Main.qml` passes provider ids to the updater, as `--except <id>` for disabled providers (line 152) and as the argument list for `retryAdvised` reruns (lines 95, 105). `wanted()` matches collector group names. In a synthetic run, `--except opencode-go` still ran the `opencode` group, and `--limits-only opencode-go` ran nothing and exited 0.

**Impact:** disabling `opencode-go` hides the tab but keeps running its collector, with the cookie, on every refresh, which contradicts the README's "Disabled agents are also skipped when the records regenerate". A `retryAdvised` flag on a fan-out record whose id differs from its group name never triggers a retry.

**Suggested change:** map ids to groups through the sidecar in `wanted()`, or document the limitation.

### Keyboard focus stays in the hidden Go field after switching tabs

Opening the card focuses the workspace field. Clicking another provider chip hides the card, but focus stays on the now-invisible field. Measured on the real `Panel.qml`: after switching to the claude tab, the field still had `activeFocus`, was not visible, and `keyCatcher.blocked` was true. By source, the panel's `h`/`l`/`j`/`k`/`r` shortcuts then go to the hidden field, and the first Escape only closes the hidden card (key presses were not synthesized).

**Impact:** after a tab switch, by source, panel shortcuts go to an invisible field and a second Escape is needed to close the panel.

**Suggested change:** close the card, or call `keyCatcher.forceActiveFocus()`, when `isGoProvider` becomes false.

### Collector names and fan-out ids are not validated

Reproduced with synthetic collectors:
- A user collector with the same name as a packaged one runs in addition to it; both write `<name>.json` and the last writer wins. #12353, which adds the same user collector directory, makes the packaged name win and tests that.
- `grep -qxF "$id"` (line 88) reads an id starting with `-` as an option, so that record is deleted on every run after the first. `grep -qxF -- "$id"` fixes it.
- An id such as `/../../../../../escape` wrote a file outside the usage directory, and retirement later removed it. An id such as `a/b` fails in `mktemp` (there is no `.a/` directory), but the run still exits 0.
- A fan-out group that once emitted a packaged id (for example `claude`) deletes that packaged record when it stops emitting it.
- Retirement only runs while a group emits a non-empty map: `{}` is rejected, and a group that switches to a single record never retires its old ids.

**Impact:** a collector's output can overwrite or delete other records, write or remove files outside the usage directory, or fail to write while the update still exits 0. User collectors are the user's own code, so this matters mainly for collectors that build ids from remote data.

**Suggested change:** validate ids against a conservative charset (for example `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, as `safeDeviceId` in `Main.qml` uses), require `.[$id].id == $id`, skip ids owned by packaged collectors, and propagate write failures to the exit status.

**Also noted:** FileView writes are asynchronous, and Apply starts the fetch without waiting for `onSaved` or handling `onSaveFailed`, so a failed write can still end in "Saved.". Starting the fetch from `onSaved` would also make the separate `mkdir` process unnecessary, since FileView creates missing parent directories itself. After a failed Test or Apply, `goFetchOk` stays false until the next Test or Apply, so the meters stay dimmed and the old failure text stays after a later refresh brings fresh numbers. The panel writes its config under `$HOME/.config`, while the updater's collector directory honours `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. The README does not mention the gear, the card, `limitsStale`, or that Go replaces the status box with a badge.

**Optional test improvement:** `agent-usage-update-test.sh` overrides `HOME` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` but not `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `XDG_CACHE_HOME`. With this PR, running it with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` exported executes the caller's real user collectors (a planted collector ran once at this head and never on the base). Setting both variables in the test, and adding cases for fan-out and retirement, would cover the new paths; none of the issues above is caught by the current tests.

**Related open PRs:**
- #11930 also sets `trailingControl` on the same `PanelHero` for its providers gear, so combining both needs one integrated control.
- #10911 prunes usage records older than seven days whose name matches no collector in `bin/` or plugin directories. It does not know the user collector directory or fan-out ids, so a user collector's records would be removed after a week without updates, for example while it keeps failing or is disabled by its group name.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head, plus sandboxed runs: the updater at base and head with synthetic collectors (flag parity, fan-out, retirement, concurrency, name and id edge cases), the existing agent tests at base, head and head merged onto current `quattro`, and the real `Panel.qml` loaded under Quickshell's offscreen platform with a stubbed popup window and synthetic Go collectors. Focus and state were measured; nothing was rendered on a desktop and no key events were synthesized. No OpenCode service was contacted and no real cookie was used. Related PRs were read from their diffs, not merged and run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
